newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil-Canada group appeals court cellphone ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil-Canada group appeals court cellphone ruling.

text.p: Telet SA on Tuesday appealed a Brazilian high court ruling last week that barred it from bidding on B Band cellular concessions in Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo state, an official said.
"They've filed an appeal with the Superior Tribunal of Justice (STJ)," said a spokeswoman for the group, which includes BCE's Bell Canada and Telesystem International Wireless Inc.

Judge Antonio de Padua Ribeiro ruled Friday in the government's favor by squashing an injunction that allowed Telet to continue bidding on the licenses, despite being disqualified by Communications Minister Sergio Motta.
In a statement, the court said Judge Ribeiro agreed with Motta's view that the consortium lacked technical experience to handle the three biggest B Band contracts.
On Monday, Telet insisted it was qualified.
"The total number of cellular telephone subscribers of Telet's three operators far exceeds the minimum 1.8 million required by the bid specifications," it said in a statement.
The statement said Telet, "reiterates its full confidence in Brazil and in the Brazilian justice system", but did not say if the group would appeal.

The injunction allowed Telet, which also includes Malaysia's TRI and Brazilian funds, to place third in an auction earlier this month for a concession covering Sao Paulo city, which was won by a group, including BellSouth Corp.
Telet remains in the running for three smaller B Band concessions.
